label: Excluded middle as a general principle: every proposition either holds or does not hold
paraphrase: Excluded middle as a general principle: every proposition either holds or does not hold (∀ p, p ∨ ¬p).

self_evident.note: Argued, not proved. Aristotle states the law (Met. IV.7, 1011b23-24) and defends it elenctically, from what the opponent grants by speaking significantly (IV.4, 1006a11-28; IV.7, 1012a17-24), not by demonstration. Lean shows without any axiom that no instance can be denied (¬¬(p ∨ ¬p); no p with ¬(p ∨ ¬p)) and that the law is equivalent to double-negation elimination. Lean does not prove excluded middle itself, and these results do not refute withholding assent (intuitionism, STMT-EXCLUDED-MIDDLE-WITHHELD-INTUITIONISM), which stays a recorded, unrefuted alternative. Scope audit: withholding remains a serious unrefuted proof/assertion-policy position, now linked to the universal assertion target. Exact global logical denial STMT-NOT-EXCLUDED-MIDDLE is separately unrefuted and is not attributed to intuitionism. The legacy floor basis and justification are retained; no-instance-denial does not independently prove global EM.
